title: Biot–Savart law and Ampère's law
qualification: AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Electricity and Magnetism (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MG05-calc-2#t3 term and clue written for the game; MG05-calc-2#t2 term and clue written for the game; MG05-calc-2#t1 term and clue written for the game; MG05-calc-2#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MG05-calc-2#N.4, MG05-calc-2#N.6, MG05-calc-2#N.10, MG05-calc-2#N.13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Solenoid
items.clue: Long coil with uniform B = μ₀nI inside and negligible B outside.

items.label: Amperian loop
items.clue: Closed path chosen for the integral, ideally with B constant along parts of it.

items.label: Ampère's law
items.clue: Says the integral of B around any closed path equals μ₀ times the current through it.

items.label: Coaxial cable
items.clue: Inner conductor carrying +I inside an outer tube carrying the reverse, so B = 0 outside.

questions.stem: A long, straight, solid cylindrical wire of radius 2.0 mm carries a steady current of 8.0 A spread uniformly over its cross section. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field inside the wire, 1.0 mm from its axis? Use μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A.

A very long, solid cylindrical conductor of radius R carries a steady current along its length. The current density is J = J₀s/R, where s is the distance from the axis and J₀ is a constant. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at a distance r < R from the axis?

A long, straight wire carrying current 2I lies along the axis of a long, thin-walled conducting cylindrical shell of radius R. The shell carries current 5I, spread uniformly around it, in the opposite direction. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at a distance r > R from the axis?

A long, thin-walled metal tube of radius R carries a steady current I along its length, spread evenly around its wall. Which describes the magnitude of the magnetic field at a distance r from the tube's axis, far from its ends?

options.text: Zero for r < R; μ₀I/(2πr) for r > R, whatever the value of R.
μ₀Ir/(2πR²) for r < R; μ₀I/(2πr) for r > R.
μ₀I/(2πR) for r < R, the value at the wall; μ₀I/(2πr) for r > R.
μ₀I/(2πr) for r < R as well, since the whole current I flows in the tube.

questions.explanation: A circle inside encloses no current, so B = 0. A circle outside encloses I, so B = μ₀I/(2πr), the same as for a thin wire on the axis: R drops out.
